pillars.title: Application security & least privilege
pillars.title_fr: Contrôlez la sécurité et limitez les droits applicatifs
pillars.summary: Confine what applications can do: mandatory access control, kernel self-protection, memory-corruption mitigations, service sandboxing.

pillars.title: Attack surface & non-essential services
pillars.title_fr: Réduisez la surface d'attaque : désactivez les services non essentiels
pillars.summary: Every listening daemon, loadable module and permissive network setting is a door. Close the ones you do not use.

pillars.title: Risky application clients
pillars.title_fr: Supprimez les clients applicatifs à risque
pillars.summary: Clear-text and legacy clients (telnet, rsh, ftp, NIS) and attacker-friendly tooling have no place on a server.

pillars.title: Server configuration integrity
pillars.summary: Know when configuration changes: integrity monitoring, strict permissions on sensitive files, protected boot chain.

pillars.title: Logging & audit trail
pillars.title_fr: Activez les logs, première étape vers la conformité
pillars.summary: No detection or accountability without persistent, tamper-resistant, time-synchronised logs and kernel audit rules.

pillars.title: SSH access
pillars.title_fr: Renforcez la sécurité et la configuration des accès SSH
pillars.summary: Audited through `sshd -T`: the configuration sshd really resolves, including Include files, drop-ins and Match blocks.

pillars.title: Privilege escalation
pillars.summary: sudo, su and setuid binaries decide who becomes root. Require re-authentication, log it, and keep the paths few.

pillars.title: Local users & groups
pillars.title_fr: Contrôlez la configuration des utilisateurs et groupes locaux
pillars.summary: One UID 0, no empty passwords, no login shell for system accounts, private homes, idle sessions that end.

pillars.title: Local password policy
pillars.title_fr: Appliquez une politique de sécurité des mots de passe utilisateurs locaux
pillars.summary: Length, reuse, lockout and hashing, checked where PAM enforces them, and on the hashes actually stored.

pillars.title: Updates & patching
pillars.title_fr: Vérifiez les mises à jour applicatives
pillars.summary: Patched on disk is not patched in memory: pending security updates, reboot debt, stale libraries, supported release.

pillars.title: Data encryption at rest
pillars.title_fr: Chiffrez vos données et les données métier de vos applications
pillars.summary: Business data, swap, crash dumps and private keys must not sit in clear text or be readable by everyone.

pillars.title: Crypto policy, FIDO & MFA
pillars.title_fr: Instaurez des politiques crypto / FIDO / MFA par OTP
pillars.summary: Strong algorithms negotiated by the real libraries, post-quantum readiness, and a second factor (OTP or FIDO2) for remote and privileged access.

pillars.title: Web services & TLS
pillars.title_fr: Sécurisez vos services web et vos certificats TLS
pillars.summary: Web servers and reverse proxies read from the configuration they resolve, and every local TLS endpoint probed like a client: no version banner or listing, no legacy TLS, no root worker, exposed admin interface or default secret, sound certificates.

pillars.title: Databases
pillars.title_fr: Protégez l'accès et la configuration de vos bases de données
pillars.summary: Database servers queried the way they apply their settings: authentication everywhere, strong password hashing, encrypted network access, no remote administrator, dangerous features off, no root process, private data directories.

pillars.title: Hardware & firmware
pillars.title_fr: Maîtrisez le matériel, le microcode et le firmware
pillars.summary: What sits under the kernel: CPU flaw mitigations and SMT, microcode, the IOMMU and DMA-capable ports, the TPM, the BMC, pending firmware updates and the USB device policy.

controls.title: A mandatory access control framework is enforcing
controls.rationale: SELinux or AppArmor confines each daemon to what its policy allows, so a compromised service cannot freely read or modify the rest of the system. Disabled or permissive MAC removes that last line of defence.
controls.check: Runtime: SELinux mode from /sys/fs/selinux/enforce, or AppArmor enabled with loaded profiles. Persistent: SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config (SELinux) and no selinux=0/apparmor=0/enforcing=0 on the next boot's kernel command line.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure SELinux mode is enforcing / Ensure all AppArmor profiles are in enforce or complain mode

remediation.summary: Enable the distribution's MAC framework in enforcing mode.
remediation.manual: RHEL-family: set SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config, run `fixfiles -F onboot` if it was disabled, reboot. Debian/Ubuntu: `apt install apparmor apparmor-utils`, make sure `apparmor=0` is not on the kernel command line, `systemctl enable --now apparmor`. Relabelling and profile tuning need a maintenance window, so Shadow-Armor does not do it automatically.

controls.title: Address space layout randomisation is fully enabled
controls.rationale: ASLR randomises stack, heap, mmap and VDSO addresses so memory-corruption exploits cannot rely on fixed addresses. Value 2 also randomises the brk heap.
controls.check: kernel.randomize_va_space: live value and the value persisted by sysctl.d/sysctl.conf.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure address space layout randomization is enabled

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.randomize_va_space = 2 in a Shadow-Armor sysctl drop-in and apply it now.

controls.title: ptrace is restricted to descendant processes
controls.rationale: Unrestricted ptrace lets any process of a user read the memory of every other process of that user (SSH agents, browsers, credential helpers). Yama scope 1 limits it to children.
controls.check: kernel.yama.ptrace_scope >= 1: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure ptrace_scope is restricted

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1 and apply it now.
remediation.risk: Debuggers can no longer attach to running processes they did not start (use sudo gdb -p).

controls.title: Kernel pointers are hidden from unprivileged users
controls.rationale: Exposed kernel addresses in /proc defeat KASLR and make kernel exploits reliable.
controls.check: kernel.kptr_restrict >= 1 (ANSSI recommends 2): live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.kptr_restrict = 2 and apply it now.

controls.title: Kernel log is restricted to privileged users
controls.rationale: dmesg leaks kernel addresses, hardware details and security events useful to an attacker.
controls.check: kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1 and apply it now.

controls.title: Unprivileged eBPF is disabled
controls.rationale: Unprivileged BPF programs have been a recurring source of local privilege escalation and speculative-execution leaks.
controls.check: kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled >= 1: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled = 1 and apply it now.

controls.title: Performance events are restricted
controls.rationale: perf_event_open exposes kernel and cross-process information and has a history of privilege-escalation bugs.
controls.check: kernel.perf_event_paranoid >= 2: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.perf_event_paranoid = 2 and apply it now.

controls.title: Symlink and hardlink protections are enabled
controls.rationale: Without them, a user can trick a privileged process into following a planted link in a shared directory (/tmp races).
controls.check: fs.protected_symlinks = 1 and fs.protected_hardlinks = 1: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist fs.protected_symlinks = 1 and fs.protected_hardlinks = 1 and apply them now.

controls.title: FIFO and regular-file protections in sticky directories
controls.rationale: Prevents opening FIFOs and regular files owned by another user in world-writable sticky directories, closing a class of data-spoofing attacks.
controls.check: fs.protected_fifos = 2 and fs.protected_regular = 2: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist fs.protected_fifos = 2 and fs.protected_regular = 2 and apply them now.

controls.title: Setuid programs cannot dump core
controls.rationale: A core dump of a privileged process can contain password hashes, keys and tokens readable by the invoking user.
controls.check: fs.suid_dumpable = 0 (live and persisted) and a hard core limit of 0 in limits.conf/limits.d.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure core dumps are restricted

remediation.summary: Persist fs.suid_dumpable = 0, set '* hard core 0' in /etc/security/limits.d/60-shadow-armor.conf.

controls.title: Loading a new kernel with kexec is disabled
controls.rationale: kexec lets root replace the running kernel without going through the boot chain, bypassing Secure Boot and lockdown.
controls.check: kernel.kexec_load_disabled = 1: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.kexec_load_disabled = 1 and apply it now (one-way until reboot).
remediation.risk: kdump crash capture stops working.

controls.title: The magic SysRq key is disabled
controls.rationale: SysRq lets anyone with console access reboot, kill processes or dump memory without authenticating.
controls.check: kernel.sysrq = 0: live and persisted.

remediation.summary: Persist kernel.sysrq = 0 and apply it now.

controls.title: Network-facing services are sandboxed by systemd
controls.rationale: A daemon that listens on the network is the first thing an attacker reaches. systemd hardening (ProtectSystem, NoNewPrivileges, capability bounding...) limits what a compromised daemon can do.
controls.check: For every unit owning a non-loopback listening socket, `systemd-analyze security` exposure must not exceed sdw_max_service_exposure.

remediation.summary: Add sandboxing directives to each exposed service with a drop-in.
remediation.manual: `systemctl edit <unit>` and add e.g. NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, ProtectKernelTunables=yes, ProtectKernelModules=yes, ProtectControlGroups=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX, CapabilityBoundingSet=, SystemCallFilter=@system-service. Re-run `systemd-analyze security <unit>` until the exposure is acceptable, then test the service.

controls.title: Hardware no-execute protection is active
controls.rationale: NX/XD marks data pages non-executable so injected shellcode cannot run. It is on by default but can be switched off on the kernel command line.
controls.check: Runtime: the CPU exposes the nx flag in /proc/cpuinfo and the running kernel was not booted with noexec=off. Persistent: the next boot's command line does not contain noexec=off.

remediation.summary: Enable NX in the firmware and remove noexec=off from the kernel command line.
remediation.manual: Enable 'Execute Disable'/'NX' in BIOS/UEFI setup; remove noexec=off from GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX (Debian) or with `grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args=noexec` (RHEL) and reboot.

controls.title: No legacy clear-text remote access server is present
controls.rationale: telnet, rsh/rlogin/rexec, tftp, talk and inetd-style super-servers send credentials in clear text and have no place on a modern host.
controls.check: Neither the packages are installed nor any of their units/sockets is active or enabled.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure telnet server services are not in use / Ensure xinetd is not installed

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask the legacy units, then remove the packages.

controls.title: mDNS/DNS-SD (Avahi) is disabled
controls.rationale: Avahi advertises the host and its services on the local network and has had remotely reachable vulnerabilities; servers do not need zero-configuration discovery.
controls.check: Units avahi-daemon.service, avahi-daemon.socket: not active now and not enabled at boot (masked or disabled).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure avahi daemon services are not in use

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask avahi-daemon.service, avahi-daemon.socket.

controls.title: The print server (CUPS) is disabled
controls.rationale: A print server listening on a server is unnecessary attack surface (CUPS browsing had critical remote bugs in 2024).
controls.check: Units cups.service, cups.socket, cups.path, cups-browsed.service: not active now and not enabled at boot (masked or disabled).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure print server services are not in use

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask cups.service, cups.socket, cups.path, cups-browsed.service.

controls.title: Only expected ports listen beyond loopback
controls.rationale: Every socket bound to a non-loopback address is reachable attack surface. The list of exposed ports must be deliberate.
controls.check: Effective: sockets the kernel reports listening now (ss -tuln) on non-loopback addresses, compared with sdw_allowed_listening_ports. UDP sockets on an ephemeral port owned by a process are the client side of an exchange (DNS, QUIC, NTP) and are ignored.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure only approved services are listening on a network interface

remediation.summary: Stop, rebind to loopback or explicitly allow each unexpected listener.
remediation.manual: For each port reported, either disable the owning service, bind it to 127.0.0.1 in its configuration, or add the port to sdw_allowed_listening_ports (`--input sdw_allowed_listening_ports=[22,443]`) if it is an intended service.

controls.title: NFS and RPC services are disabled
controls.rationale: rpcbind and the NFS server expose RPC services to the network; disable them unless the host is a file server.
controls.check: Units rpcbind.service, rpcbind.socket, nfs-server.service, nfs-kernel-server.service: not active now and not enabled at boot (masked or disabled).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure rpcbind services are not in use / Ensure nfs server services are not in use

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask rpcbind.service, rpcbind.socket, nfs-server.service, nfs-kernel-server.service.

controls.title: The SNMP daemon is disabled
controls.rationale: SNMP v1/v2c authenticates with clear-text community strings and leaks detailed system information.
controls.check: Units snmpd.service: not active now and not enabled at boot (masked or disabled).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure snmp services are not in use

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask snmpd.service.

controls.title: The mail transfer agent only listens locally
controls.rationale: A local MTA is often needed for system mail, but it must not accept connections from the network.
controls.check: No mail transfer agent installed (durable), or, when one is, no socket on port 25/465/587 bound to a non-loopback address (live).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure mail transfer agent is configured for local-only mode

remediation.summary: Bind the MTA to loopback.
remediation.manual: Postfix: `postconf -e inet_interfaces=loopback-only && systemctl restart postfix`. Exim (Debian): dc_local_interfaces='127.0.0.1 ; ::1' in /etc/exim4/update-exim4.conf.conf, then `update-exim4.conf`. Sendmail: DAEMON_OPTIONS Addr=127.0.0.1.

controls.title: Uncommon filesystem modules cannot be loaded
controls.rationale: Rarely used filesystem drivers are poorly audited kernel code reachable by mounting crafted media or images.
controls.check: For cramfs, freevxfs, hfs, hfsplus, jffs2, udf: not loaded now, and the effective modprobe configuration (`modprobe --showconfig`) turns loading into a no-op (or the module does not exist).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure cramfs/freevxfs/hfs/hfsplus/jffs2/udf kernel module is not available

remediation.summary: Write 'install <module> /bin/false' and 'blacklist <module>' for each module to /etc/modprobe.d/60-shadow-armor.conf and unload them.

controls.title: Uncommon network protocol modules cannot be loaded
controls.rationale: DCCP, SCTP, RDS and TIPC are auto-loaded by an unprivileged socket() call and have produced several remote and local kernel exploits.
controls.check: For dccp, sctp, rds, tipc: not loaded now and made unloadable by the effective modprobe configuration.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure dccp/sctp/rds/tipc kernel module is not available

remediation.summary: Disable the modules in /etc/modprobe.d/60-shadow-armor.conf and unload them.

controls.title: USB mass storage cannot be used
controls.rationale: USB storage is a data-exfiltration and malware-introduction path on servers that never need it.
controls.check: usb-storage: not loaded now and made unloadable by the effective modprobe configuration.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure usb-storage kernel module is not available

remediation.summary: Disable usb-storage in /etc/modprobe.d/60-shadow-armor.conf and unload it.
remediation.risk: USB keys and disks will no longer mount on this host.

controls.title: IP forwarding is disabled
controls.rationale: A host that forwards packets can be abused as a router between networks it should isolate. Container hosts and routers legitimately need it: waive the control there.
controls.check: net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0 and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure ip forwarding is disabled

remediation.summary: Persist forwarding = 0 for IPv4 and IPv6 and apply it now.
remediation.risk: Breaks container networking (Docker, Kubernetes, LXC), VM bridges, VPN gateways and routers: the harden refuses when it finds one of them; waive the control on such hosts.

controls.title: ICMP redirects are neither accepted nor sent
controls.rationale: Accepted redirects let an attacker on the local network rewrite the routing table (man-in-the-middle); sending them is only for routers.
controls.check: accept_redirects, secure_redirects and send_redirects are 0 for all/default interfaces (IPv4 and IPv6): live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure icmp redirects are not accepted / Ensure packet redirect sending is disabled

remediation.summary: Persist the redirect settings and apply them now.

controls.title: Source-routed packets are refused
controls.rationale: Source routing lets the sender choose the path of a packet, which can be used to bypass network filtering.
controls.check: accept_source_route = 0 for all/default interfaces (IPv4 and IPv6): live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure source routed packets are not accepted

remediation.summary: Persist the source-route settings and apply them now.

controls.title: Strict reverse-path filtering is enabled
controls.rationale: Reverse-path filtering drops packets whose source address could not be routed back through the receiving interface, defeating IP spoofing.
controls.check: net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1 and net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 1: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure reverse path filtering is enabled

remediation.summary: Persist rp_filter = 1 and apply it now.
remediation.risk: Asymmetric routing setups (multiple uplinks) may drop legitimate traffic.

controls.title: TCP SYN cookies are enabled
controls.rationale: SYN cookies keep the host reachable during a SYN flood.
controls.check: net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure tcp syn cookies is enabled

remediation.summary: Persist net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1 and apply it now.

controls.title: Broadcast pings and bogus ICMP errors are ignored
controls.rationale: Answering broadcast echo requests makes the host a Smurf-attack amplifier; bogus ICMP error responses fill the logs.
controls.check: net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts = 1 and net.ipv4.icmp_ignore_bogus_error_responses = 1: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure broadcast icmp requests are ignored / Ensure bogus icmp responses are ignored

remediation.summary: Persist both settings and apply them now.

controls.title: Martian packets are logged
controls.rationale: Packets with impossible source addresses reveal spoofing attempts or misconfigured networks; logging them feeds detection.
controls.check: net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians = 1 and net.ipv4.conf.default.log_martians = 1: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure suspicious packets are logged

remediation.summary: Persist log_martians = 1 and apply it now.

controls.title: IPv6 router advertisements are refused
controls.rationale: Rogue router advertisements let anyone on the segment reroute or intercept IPv6 traffic. Static servers should not auto-configure routes.
controls.check: net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra = 0 and net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0: live and persisted.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure ipv6 router advertisements are not accepted

remediation.summary: Persist accept_ra = 0 and apply it now.
remediation.risk: Hosts that rely on SLAAC for IPv6 addressing or default route lose IPv6 connectivity.

controls.title: A host firewall denies inbound traffic by default
controls.rationale: A default-deny inbound policy turns every forgotten or accidentally started service into an unreachable one.
controls.check: Runtime: the kernel ruleset (nftables, iptables or ufw) has an input chain with a drop/reject policy or catch-all rule. Persistent: a firewall service that restores it at boot is enabled.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure a single firewall configuration utility is in use / Ensure default deny firewall policy

remediation.summary: Install and enable ufw (Debian/Ubuntu) or firewalld (RHEL-family) with default-deny inbound, keeping open every port that listens now, the effective sshd ports and sdw_allowed_listening_ports.
remediation.risk: Inbound traffic to ports nothing listens on now is dropped; every port listening now stays open (listed before applying). Refused on Kubernetes nodes, Proxmox VE hosts and hosts managed by another firewall.

controls.title: /tmp is mounted with nodev,nosuid,noexec
controls.rationale: World-writable /tmp is where attackers drop payloads. Mounting it separately with nodev, nosuid, noexec stops device files, setuid binaries and direct execution from it.
controls.check: Runtime: /tmp is a separate mount carrying nodev, nosuid, noexec in /proc/self/mounts. Persistent: the /etc/fstab entry (or systemd mount unit) that mounts it at boot carries the same options.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure /tmp is a separate partition / Ensure nodev, nosuid, noexec option set on /tmp partition

remediation.summary: Add nodev,nosuid,noexec to the /tmp mount (fstab entry or systemd mount drop-in) and remount it live.
remediation.risk: noexec can break installers or tools that execute from the mount point (set TMPDIR for them). When /tmp is not a separate mount yet, tmp.mount is enabled: it mounts at the next reboot, or earlier when a service using PrivateTmp restarts, hiding what /tmp held.

controls.title: /dev/shm is mounted with nodev,nosuid,noexec
controls.rationale: World-writable /dev/shm is where attackers drop payloads. Mounting it separately with nodev, nosuid, noexec stops device files, setuid binaries and direct execution from it.
controls.check: Runtime: /dev/shm is a separate mount carrying nodev, nosuid, noexec in /proc/self/mounts. Persistent: the /etc/fstab entry (or systemd mount unit) that mounts it at boot carries the same options.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure nodev, nosuid, noexec option set on /dev/shm partition

remediation.summary: Add nodev,nosuid,noexec to the /dev/shm mount (fstab entry or systemd mount drop-in) and remount it live.
remediation.risk: noexec on /dev/shm breaks software that executes code from shared memory (some JIT runtimes, headless browsers).

controls.title: /var/tmp is mounted with nodev,nosuid,noexec
controls.rationale: World-writable /var/tmp is where attackers drop payloads. Mounting it separately with nodev, nosuid, noexec stops device files, setuid binaries and direct execution from it.
controls.check: Runtime: /var/tmp is a separate mount carrying nodev, nosuid, noexec in /proc/self/mounts. Persistent: the /etc/fstab entry (or systemd mount unit) that mounts it at boot carries the same options.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure /var/tmp is a separate partition / Ensure nodev, nosuid, noexec option set on /var/tmp partition

remediation.summary: Add nodev,nosuid,noexec to the /var/tmp mount (fstab entry or systemd mount drop-in) and remount it live.
remediation.risk: noexec can break installers or tools that execute from /var/tmp. When /var/tmp is not a separate mount, nothing changes (manual).

controls.title: The automounter (autofs) is disabled
controls.rationale: autofs mounts removable and network media on access, a path for malicious media and data exfiltration.
controls.check: Units autofs.service: not active now and not enabled at boot (masked or disabled).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure autofs services are not in use

remediation.summary: Stop, disable and mask autofs.service.

controls.title: Ctrl-Alt-Del does not reboot the host
controls.rationale: Anyone with console access (physical or through a hypervisor console) could reboot the host without authenticating.
controls.check: ctrl-alt-del.target is masked (persistent) and not active (runtime).

remediation.summary: Mask ctrl-alt-del.target.

controls.title: No X11 display server is installed
controls.rationale: A graphical stack brings hundreds of packages and setuid helpers a server never uses.
controls.check: No xserver-xorg*/xorg-x11-server* package installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure X window server services are not in use

remediation.summary: Remove the X server packages.
remediation.risk: Removes any graphical desktop installed on the host.

controls.title: The telnet client is not installed
controls.rationale: telnet sends everything, passwords included, in clear text; its presence invites its use.
controls.check: None of telnet, inetutils-telnet is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure telnet client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove telnet, inetutils-telnet.

controls.title: rsh/rlogin clients are not installed
controls.rationale: The r-commands authenticate by host name and transmit in clear text.
controls.check: None of rsh-client, rsh-redone-client, rsh is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure rsh client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove rsh-client, rsh-redone-client, rsh.

controls.title: The NIS client is not installed
controls.rationale: NIS distributes password hashes and maps in clear text to anyone who asks.
controls.check: None of nis, ypbind, yp-tools, ypbind-mt is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure nis client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove nis, ypbind, yp-tools, ypbind-mt.

controls.title: The talk client is not installed
controls.rationale: talk is an unauthenticated legacy messaging protocol.
controls.check: None of talk, inetutils-talk is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure talk client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove talk, inetutils-talk.

controls.title: FTP and TFTP clients are not installed
controls.rationale: FTP and TFTP move files, and FTP credentials, in clear text; use SFTP/SCP instead.
controls.check: None of ftp, tnftp, inetutils-ftp, lftp, tftp, tftp-hpa, atftp is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure ftp client is not installed / Ensure tftp client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove ftp, tnftp, inetutils-ftp, lftp, tftp, tftp-hpa, atftp.

controls.title: LDAP command-line clients are not installed
controls.rationale: ldapsearch and friends make directory reconnaissance trivial for an intruder and are rarely needed on servers.
controls.check: None of ldap-utils, openldap-clients is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure ldap client is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove ldap-utils, openldap-clients.

controls.title: No netcat variant with command execution is installed
controls.rationale: netcat-traditional supports -e, the classic one-liner to hand an attacker a remote shell.
controls.check: None of netcat-traditional is installed.

remediation.summary: Remove netcat-traditional.

controls.title: No compiler toolchain is installed on the server
controls.rationale: A compiler lets an intruder build local exploits on the spot. Build on dedicated build hosts.
controls.check: None of gcc, g++, clang, tcc, gcc-c++ is installed.

remediation.summary: Remove gcc, g++, clang, tcc, gcc-c++.

controls.title: prelink is not installed
controls.rationale: prelink rewrites binaries in place, which defeats integrity monitoring and weakens ASLR.
controls.check: None of prelink is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure prelink is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove prelink.

controls.title: SELinux troubleshooting daemons are not installed
controls.rationale: setroubleshoot and mcstrans run extra privileged daemons that are only useful while developing policy.
controls.check: None of setroubleshoot, setroubleshoot-server, mcstrans is installed.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure SETroubleshoot is not installed / Ensure the MCS Translation Service (mcstrans) is not installed

remediation.summary: Remove setroubleshoot, setroubleshoot-server, mcstrans.

controls.title: The SSH client does not forward agents or X11 by default
controls.rationale: A forwarded agent lets root on any server you connect to use your keys; forwarded X11 lets it read your keystrokes. Enable them per trusted host only.
controls.check: Effective client configuration (`ssh -G` for an arbitrary host, which resolves ssh_config and its Include files): forwardagent no and forwardx11 no.

remediation.summary: Write ForwardAgent no / ForwardX11 no at the top of the system ssh_config through a drop-in.

actions.content:
# Managed by Shadow-Armor (SA-03.11)
Host *
    ForwardAgent no
    ForwardX11 no

controls.title: File integrity monitoring is installed and initialised
controls.rationale: Without a baseline of file hashes, a replaced binary or modified configuration goes unnoticed.
controls.check: AIDE is installed and its database exists (aide.db / aide.db.gz in the configured location).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure AIDE is installed

remediation.summary: Install AIDE and initialise its database.
remediation.risk: Initialisation hashes the whole system and can take several minutes.

controls.title: File integrity is checked periodically
controls.rationale: An integrity database nobody compares against detects nothing.
controls.check: A scheduled AIDE check exists: an enabled aidecheck/dailyaidecheck timer, or a cron entry running aide --check.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure filesystem integrity is regularly checked

remediation.summary: Install and enable a daily aide --check systemd timer.

actions.content:
# Managed by Shadow-Armor (SA-04.02)
[Unit]
Description=Shadow-Armor AIDE integrity check

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'command -v aide >/dev/null && aide --check --config=$( [ -f /etc/aide/aide.conf ] && echo /etc/aide/aide.conf || echo /etc/aide.conf )'
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle

# Managed by Shadow-Armor (SA-04.02)
[Unit]
Description=Daily AIDE integrity check

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
RandomizedDelaySec=1h
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

controls.title: Account database files have safe permissions
controls.rationale: /etc/passwd and /etc/group must be readable by all but writable only by root.
controls.check: /etc/passwd and /etc/group: mode <= 0644, owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on /etc/passwd are configured / Ensure permissions on /etc/group are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits and set owner root.

controls.title: Password hash files are not readable by users
controls.rationale: Readable /etc/shadow hands every password hash to offline cracking.
controls.check: /etc/shadow and /etc/gshadow: mode <= 0640, owner root, group root or shadow.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured / Ensure permissions on /etc/gshadow are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits and set owner root.

controls.title: Backup account files have safe permissions
controls.rationale: passwd-, shadow-, group- and gshadow- are copies of the account databases and deserve the same protection.
controls.check: /etc/passwd- and /etc/group- <= 0644; /etc/shadow- and /etc/gshadow- <= 0640; owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow- are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits and set owner root.

controls.title: The boot loader configuration is readable by root only
controls.rationale: grub.cfg reveals kernel parameters and, when set, the boot password hash.
controls.check: grub.cfg (/boot/grub/grub.cfg or /boot/grub2/grub.cfg, and user.cfg): mode <= 0600, owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure access to bootloader config is configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits from the grub configuration.

controls.title: A boot loader password is set
controls.rationale: Without it, anyone at the console can edit the kernel command line (init=/bin/sh) and bypass every control on this host.
controls.check: grub.cfg or user.cfg declares a superuser with a PBKDF2 password.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure bootloader password is set

remediation.summary: Set a GRUB superuser password.
remediation.manual: RHEL-family: `grub2-setpassword`. Debian/Ubuntu: `grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2`, then add `set superusers="root"` and `password_pbkdf2 root <hash>` to /etc/grub.d/40_custom and run `update-grub`. Keep the password in your vault: it is needed to edit boot entries.

controls.title: cron configuration is writable and readable by root only
controls.rationale: Anyone who can write a cron file runs code as root; anyone who can read it learns what runs when.
controls.check: /etc/crontab <= 0600 and /etc/cron.d, cron.hourly, cron.daily, cron.weekly, cron.monthly <= 0700, owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on /etc/crontab are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits from the cron files and directories.

controls.title: cron and at are restricted to allowlisted users
controls.rationale: Only named users should be able to schedule jobs; an allowlist is safer than a denylist.
controls.check: /etc/cron.allow exists (mode <= 0640, owner root) and, when at is installed, /etc/at.allow exists.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure crontab is restricted to authorized users / Ensure at is restricted to authorized users

remediation.summary: Create /etc/cron.allow (and /etc/at.allow when at is installed) listing root and every user that has a crontab now.
remediation.risk: Other users can no longer create crontabs or at jobs until they are added to the allow files; existing crontabs keep running.

controls.title: UEFI Secure Boot is enabled
controls.rationale: Secure Boot verifies the boot loader and kernel signatures, blocking bootkits and unsigned kernel modules (with lockdown).
controls.check: On UEFI hosts, the SecureBoot EFI variable is set (mokutil --sb-state or efivarfs). Skipped on BIOS hosts and containers.

remediation.summary: Enable Secure Boot in the firmware.
remediation.manual: Enter the UEFI setup, enable Secure Boot with the distribution's shim/keys (or your own enrolled keys), and verify with `mokutil --sb-state`.

controls.title: Kernel lockdown is active
controls.rationale: Lockdown prevents even root from modifying the running kernel (raw memory, unsigned modules, kexec), protecting integrity after compromise.
controls.check: /sys/kernel/security/lockdown selects integrity or confidentiality now, and the next boot keeps it: lockdown= on the boot loader command line, a kernel built to force lockdown, or Secure Boot with a kernel that locks down under it.

remediation.summary: Boot with lockdown=integrity (usually implied by Secure Boot).
remediation.manual: Add `lockdown=integrity` to the kernel command line (and enable Secure Boot), then reboot.

controls.title: No world-writable files exist on local filesystems
controls.rationale: A world-writable file (script, config, library) lets any local user alter what others, including root, execute or read.
controls.check: Single-pass scan of local filesystems (container and VM storage skipped: Docker, containerd, kubelet, LXC/LXD/Incus, Proxmox guest volumes, libvirt) (find -xdev) for regular files with the o+w bit.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured

remediation.summary: Remove the world-write bit from the files found by the scan.

controls.title: World-writable directories have the sticky bit
controls.rationale: Without the sticky bit, any user can delete or replace other users' files in a shared directory.
controls.check: Single-pass scan of local filesystems (container and VM storage skipped: Docker, containerd, kubelet, LXC/LXD/Incus, Proxmox guest volumes, libvirt) for directories with o+w but not +t.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured

remediation.summary: Add the sticky bit to the directories found by the scan.

controls.title: No file lacks a valid owner or group
controls.rationale: Files owned by a deleted UID/GID are silently inherited by the next account created with that ID.
controls.check: Single-pass scan of local filesystems (container and VM storage skipped: Docker, containerd, kubelet, LXC/LXD/Incus, Proxmox guest volumes, libvirt) for -nouser or -nogroup.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure no files or directories without an owner and a group exist

remediation.summary: Assign or remove each orphaned file.
remediation.manual: Review each listed path, then `chown root:root <path>` or delete it.

controls.title: A system logger is running and enabled
controls.rationale: Without a running logger, authentication failures, service crashes and kernel events vanish.
controls.check: systemd-journald, rsyslog or syslog-ng: active now and enabled (or static) at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure journald service is enabled and active / Ensure rsyslog service is enabled and active

remediation.summary: Install and enable rsyslog when no logger is enabled.

controls.title: The systemd journal is written to disk
controls.rationale: A volatile journal loses every log line at reboot, typically the moment an investigation needs them.
controls.check: Effective journald configuration (`systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/journald.conf`, drop-ins merged): Storage=persistent, or Storage=auto with /var/log/journal present.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure journald is configured to write logfiles to persistent disk

remediation.summary: Set Storage=persistent in a journald drop-in and restart systemd-journald.

controls.title: The audit daemon is installed, running and enabled
controls.rationale: auditd records security-relevant kernel events (identity changes, privilege use, module loading) that ordinary logs never see.
controls.check: auditd: installed, active now, enabled at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure auditd packages are installed / Ensure auditd service is enabled and active

remediation.summary: Install the audit daemon and enable it.

controls.title: Processes started before auditd are audited
controls.rationale: Without audit=1 on the kernel command line, events from early boot processes are never recorded.
controls.check: audit=1 on the running kernel's command line (runtime) and on the next boot's command line (persistent).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure auditing for processes that start prior to auditd is enabled

remediation.summary: Add audit=1 to the boot loader's kernel command line.

controls.title: The audit backlog is large enough
controls.rationale: An undersized backlog drops audit events under load, precisely when an attack generates many.
controls.check: audit_backlog_limit >= 8192 on the running kernel and on the next boot's command line.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is sufficient

remediation.summary: Add audit_backlog_limit=8192 to the boot loader's kernel command line.

controls.title: Changes to users and groups are audited
controls.rationale: Account creation, password changes and group membership changes are the first steps of persistence.
controls.check: Write/attribute watches on /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /etc/shadow, /etc/gshadow, /etc/security/opasswd. Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure events that modify user/group information are collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: Changes to sudo rules are audited
controls.rationale: A new sudoers line is a silent, permanent root backdoor.
controls.check: Write/attribute watches on /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d. Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: Commands run as another user are audited
controls.rationale: Every execution where the effective UID differs from the login UID (sudo, su, setuid) must be attributable to a person.
controls.check: execve rules with -C euid!=uid for b64 and b32. Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure actions as another user are always logged

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

rules: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -C euid!=uid -F auid!=unset -S execve -k user_emulation
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -C euid!=uid -F auid!=unset -S execve -k user_emulation

controls.title: Changes to the system time are audited
controls.rationale: Tampering with the clock breaks log correlation and certificate validation.
controls.check: adjtimex, settimeofday and clock_settime syscall rules (b64) and a watch on /etc/localtime. Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure events that modify date and time information are collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: Kernel module loading is audited
controls.rationale: Loading a kernel module is how rootkits install themselves.
controls.check: init_module, finit_module and delete_module syscall rules (b64). Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure kernel module loading unloading and modification is collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: Login and logout events are audited
controls.rationale: Changes to lastlog and faillock records reveal logins and brute-force attempts.
controls.check: Watches on /var/log/lastlog and /var/run/faillock. Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure login and logout events are collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: Changes to the MAC policy are audited
controls.rationale: Weakening SELinux/AppArmor policy is a precursor to bypassing it.
controls.check: Watches on /etc/selinux and /etc/apparmor(.d). Runtime: rules loaded in the kernel (`auditctl -l`). Persistent: rules in /etc/audit/rules.d loaded at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure events that modify the system's Mandatory Access Controls are collected

remediation.summary: Add the rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/60-shadow-armor.rules and load them (augenrules --load).

controls.title: The audit configuration is immutable
controls.rationale: With -e 2, even root cannot disable or alter audit rules without a reboot, which itself is logged.
controls.check: Runtime: auditctl -s reports enabled 2. Persistent: the last loaded rule file ends with -e 2.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure the audit configuration is immutable

remediation.summary: Add -e 2 as the final audit rule (effective after the next reboot).

controls.title: The host fails safe when audit storage runs out
controls.rationale: If the audit volume fills up, auditd must not silently stop recording.
controls.check: auditd.conf: max_log_file_action is keep_logs or rotate, space_left_action is email/exec/single/halt, admin_space_left_action and disk_full_action are single or halt.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure system is disabled when audit logs are full / Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted

remediation.summary: Set the storage actions in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and reload auditd.
remediation.risk: The host drops to single-user mode if the audit partition fills up; size /var/log/audit accordingly.

controls.title: Audit logs are protected from other users
controls.rationale: Audit trails must be readable only by administrators and writable only by auditd.
controls.check: Audit log directory <= 0750 and log files <= 0640, owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure audit log files mode is configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits from /var/log/audit.

controls.title: Logs are forwarded to a remote collector
controls.rationale: Logs kept only on the host are the first thing an intruder with root erases.
controls.check: Effective rsyslog/syslog-ng configuration forwards to a remote host (omfwd/@@/@ or destination network), or systemd-journal-upload is enabled.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host

remediation.summary: Forward logs to your collector.
remediation.manual: rsyslog: create /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf with `*.* action(type="omfwd" target="logs.example.org" port="6514" protocol="tcp" StreamDriver="gtls" StreamDriverMode="1")` and restart rsyslog; or configure systemd-journal-upload. Shadow-Armor cannot guess your collector address.

controls.title: Time is synchronised
controls.rationale: Log correlation, Kerberos and TLS all depend on an accurate clock.
controls.check: chronyd, systemd-timesyncd or ntpd: active now and enabled at boot.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure time synchronization is in use

remediation.summary: Install and enable chrony.

controls.title: Root cannot log in over SSH with a password
controls.rationale: A root password reachable over SSH is the first target of brute force: one guessed password gives full control of the host. With PermitRootLogin prohibit-password (the OpenSSH default), root can still log in with an SSH key, which cannot be guessed, and never with a password.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T permitrootlogin is no, prohibit-password (sshd prints it as without-password) or forced-commands-only. yes fails.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled (root password logins; SA-06.21 covers key logins)

remediation.summary: Set PermitRootLogin prohibit-password in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in (root keeps its key logins), validate with sshd -t and reload sshd.
remediation.risk: Root can no longer log in over SSH with a password. Key logins keep working: the harden checks that root has a key, or that an administrator account can reach root, before applying.

controls.title: No SSH login path relies on a password alone
controls.rationale: Password-only SSH is brute-forced continuously on every internet-facing host. Keys, or a password plus a second factor, remove that risk.
controls.check: Effective: passwordauthentication = no and keyboard-interactive either disabled or backed by a second factor, or every AuthenticationMethods list requires publickey.

remediation.summary: Set PasswordAuthentication no and KbdInteractiveAuthentication no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.
remediation.risk: Users without an authorized key are locked out of SSH.

controls.title: SSH refuses empty passwords
controls.rationale: An account with an empty password would be reachable over the network with no credential at all.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T permitemptypasswords = no.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled

remediation.summary: Set PermitEmptyPasswords no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH limits authentication attempts per connection
controls.rationale: A low MaxAuthTries slows brute force and forces attackers to reconnect, which fail2ban-style tools catch.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T maxauthtries <= sdw_ssh_max_auth_tries.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd MaxAuthTries is configured

remediation.summary: Set MaxAuthTries in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.
remediation.risk: Clients that offer many keys from their agent can hit the limit before the right one: point them at it (IdentityFile with IdentitiesOnly yes).

controls.title: Unauthenticated SSH connections time out quickly
controls.rationale: A long LoginGraceTime lets an attacker hold many unauthenticated connections open and exhaust MaxStartups.
controls.check: Effective: 0 < logingracetime <= sdw_ssh_login_grace_time.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd LoginGraceTime is configured

remediation.summary: Set LoginGraceTime in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: Unresponsive SSH clients are disconnected
controls.rationale: sshd probes the client every ClientAliveInterval seconds and closes the session after ClientAliveCountMax unanswered probes: a session whose client vanished (network cut, laptop closed) does not stay open for hours. It does not close a session whose client is merely idle: TMOUT (SA-08.13) does.
controls.check: Effective: clientaliveinterval > 0 and clientaliveinterval x clientalivecountmax <= sdw_ssh_idle_timeout_max (seconds before a silent client is dropped).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are configured

remediation.summary: Set ClientAliveInterval 300 and ClientAliveCountMax 3 in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH X11 forwarding is disabled
controls.rationale: X11 forwarding exposes the client's display to the server: a compromised server can read keystrokes on the admin workstation.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T x11forwarding = no.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd X11Forwarding is disabled

remediation.summary: Set X11Forwarding no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH TCP forwarding is disabled
controls.rationale: Port forwarding turns an SSH account into a tunnel through your network filtering.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T allowtcpforwarding = no (or disableforwarding = yes).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd AllowTcpForwarding is disabled

remediation.summary: Set AllowTcpForwarding no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.
remediation.risk: Breaks SSH tunnels and remote development tools relying on port forwarding.

controls.title: SSH host-based trust is disabled
controls.rationale: Host-based authentication and .rhosts files trust a machine instead of a person.
controls.check: Effective: hostbasedauthentication = no and ignorerhosts = yes.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd HostbasedAuthentication is disabled / Ensure sshd IgnoreRhosts is enabled

remediation.summary: Set HostbasedAuthentication no and IgnoreRhosts yes in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH ignores user-supplied environment
controls.rationale: PermitUserEnvironment lets users set LD_PRELOAD-style variables for sshd-spawned processes, bypassing restrictions such as ForceCommand.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T permituserenvironment = no.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd PermitUserEnvironment is disabled

remediation.summary: Set PermitUserEnvironment no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH logs enough to identify who logged in with which key
controls.rationale: INFO is the minimum; VERBOSE also records the fingerprint of the key used, which attributes a login to a key.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T loglevel is INFO or VERBOSE.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd LogLevel is configured

remediation.summary: Set LogLevel VERBOSE in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH access is limited to named users or groups
controls.rationale: An allowlist ensures that service and forgotten accounts cannot log in over SSH even if they get a password or key.
controls.check: Effective: at least one of allowusers, allowgroups, denyusers, denygroups is set.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd access is configured

remediation.summary: Declare who may log in over SSH.
remediation.manual: Create a group (e.g. `groupadd sshusers`), add the administrators, then set `AllowGroups sshusers` in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-shadow-armor.conf (or your own drop-in) and reload sshd. Test from a second session before closing the first one.

controls.title: SSH shows a legal warning banner
controls.rationale: A warning banner supports prosecution and satisfies notice requirements; it must not reveal the OS version.
controls.check: Effective: banner points to an existing file that does not contain \m, \r, \s or \v escapes.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd Banner is configured

remediation.summary: Write a neutral /etc/issue.net and set Banner /etc/issue.net in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

actions.content: Authorized access only. All activity may be monitored and reported.

controls.title: SSH authentication goes through PAM
controls.rationale: PAM is where account lockout, password policy and second factors are enforced; bypassing it disables them for SSH.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T usepam = yes.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd UsePAM is enabled

remediation.summary: Set UsePAM yes in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH limits concurrent unauthenticated connections and sessions
controls.rationale: MaxStartups throttles connection floods; MaxSessions limits multiplexed shells per connection.
controls.check: Effective: maxstartups start:rate:full no looser than 10:30:60 and maxsessions <= sdw_ssh_max_sessions.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd MaxStartups is configured / Ensure sshd MaxSessions is configured

remediation.summary: Set MaxStartups 10:30:60 and MaxSessions in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: SSH GSSAPI authentication is disabled
controls.rationale: Unused authentication methods are unneeded attack surface in sshd's pre-authentication code.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T gssapiauthentication = no.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd GSSAPIAuthentication is disabled

remediation.summary: Set GSSAPIAuthentication no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.
remediation.risk: Breaks Kerberos single sign-on over SSH.

controls.title: No SSH Match block relaxes a hardened setting
controls.rationale: A Match block (for an address, user or group) silently overrides the global configuration for matching connections: a hardened global config can be defeated by one permissive Match.
controls.check: Every Match block reachable from sshd_config (Include files and drop-ins walked in sshd order) is checked for PermitRootLogin yes, PasswordAuthentication/PermitEmptyPasswords/PermitUserEnvironment/HostbasedAuthentication yes, or AuthenticationMethods any.

remediation.summary: Remove the relaxing keywords from the Match blocks listed.
remediation.manual: Edit the file:line reported, drop the permissive keyword (or restrict the Match to a management network and document a waiver), then `sshd -t && systemctl reload ssh`.

controls.title: sshd configuration files are writable by root only
controls.rationale: Whoever can edit sshd_config or a drop-in controls who logs in.
controls.check: /etc/ssh/sshd_config and /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*: mode <= 0600, owner root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits.

controls.title: SSH host private keys are protected
controls.rationale: A readable host key lets anyone impersonate the server and intercept every SSH session.
controls.check: /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key: mode <= 0640, owner root, group root or ssh_keys.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure permissions on SSH private host key files are configured

remediation.summary: Remove excess permission bits from the host keys.

controls.title: sshd checks home and key file permissions
controls.rationale: StrictModes refuses keys whose files or parent directories are writable by others, which would let anyone add their own key.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T strictmodes = yes.

remediation.summary: Set StrictModes yes in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in.

controls.title: Root cannot log in over SSH at all
controls.rationale: Administrators who log in with their own account and then use sudo leave a trace of who did what; a shared root login does not. Refusing root also takes the most valuable account off the network entirely, keys included.
controls.check: Effective: sshd -T permitrootlogin = no, and no Match block lets root log in again.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled

remediation.summary: Set PermitRootLogin no in the Shadow-Armor sshd drop-in, validate with sshd -t and reload sshd.
remediation.risk: Root can no longer log in over SSH, even with a key: administrators log in with their own account and use sudo. The harden refuses when no such account can log in with a key and use sudo, or when you are connected as root.

controls.title: sudo runs commands in a pseudo-terminal
controls.rationale: use_pty stops a command run through sudo from injecting keystrokes into the user's terminal after sudo returns (TIOCSTI).
controls.check: Effective sudoers Defaults (main file and every include, last one wins): use_pty set.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sudo commands use pty

remediation.summary: Add 'Defaults use_pty' to /etc/sudoers.d/zz-shadow-armor (validated with visudo).

controls.title: sudo keeps a dedicated log
controls.rationale: A dedicated sudo log makes privileged activity easy to review and forward.
controls.check: Effective sudoers Defaults: logfile is set.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sudo log file exists

remediation.summary: Add 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo.log"' to /etc/sudoers.d/zz-shadow-armor.

controls.title: sudo requires re-authentication
controls.rationale: NOPASSWD or !authenticate means that anyone who hijacks the user's session (stolen key, browser exploit, shared terminal) is instantly root.
controls.check: No NOPASSWD tag in any sudoers rule and no Defaults !authenticate, across all included files.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure users must provide password for privilege escalation / Ensure re-authentication for privilege escalation is not disabled globally

remediation.summary: Remove NOPASSWD and !authenticate from the listed sudoers lines.
remediation.manual: Edit each listed file with `visudo -f <file>`. Cloud images often grant the default user NOPASSWD in /etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users: set a password for that user first (`passwd <user>`), then remove the tag. Automation accounts that truly need it should get a narrow command list and a waiver.

controls.title: sudo credential caching is short
controls.rationale: A long timestamp_timeout keeps a window where any process of the user can become root without a password.
controls.check: Effective sudoers Defaults: timestamp_timeout between 0 and 15 minutes (the sudo default is 5 when unset).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure sudo authentication timeout is configured correctly

remediation.summary: Set 'Defaults timestamp_timeout=5' in /etc/sudoers.d/zz-shadow-armor.

controls.title: su is restricted to a dedicated group
controls.rationale: Without pam_wheel, any user who learns the root password can become root with su.
controls.check: Effective PAM auth stack of su includes pam_wheel.so with use_uid.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure access to the su command is restricted

remediation.summary: Create an empty 'sugroup' group and require it in /etc/pam.d/su (auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=sugroup).
remediation.risk: Only members of 'sugroup' (none initially) can use su: the harden refuses when a user relies on su because nobody can use sudo.

controls.title: sudoers files are owned by root and not writable by others
controls.rationale: A sudoers file writable by anyone but root is a direct path to root.
controls.check: /etc/sudoers and every included file: owner root, mode <= 0440.

remediation.summary: Set owner root and remove excess permission bits.

controls.title: sudo rules do not rely on command negation
controls.rationale: 'ALL, !/bin/su' is trivially bypassed by copying or renaming the binary; negation gives a false sense of restriction.
controls.check: No sudoers rule grants commands with a '!' negation.

remediation.summary: Replace negated command lists with explicit allowlists.
remediation.manual: Rewrite each listed rule to name exactly the commands (with arguments) the user needs.

controls.title: sudo sanitises the environment
controls.rationale: Keeping the caller's environment (LD_PRELOAD, PATH, PYTHONPATH...) lets a user steer what root executes.
controls.check: Effective sudoers Defaults: env_reset is not disabled and secure_path is set.

remediation.summary: Add 'Defaults env_reset' and a standard secure_path to /etc/sudoers.d/zz-shadow-armor.

controls.title: setuid/setgid binaries are limited to an allowlist
controls.rationale: Every setuid-root binary is a potential privilege escalation (PwnKit, sudo Baron Samedit). Unknown ones must be justified.
controls.check: Single-pass filesystem scan (container and VM storage skipped) for setuid/setgid files, compared with sdw_suid_allowlist.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure SUID and SGID files are reviewed

remediation.summary: Remove the setuid/setgid bit from binaries you do not need.
remediation.manual: For each listed file, `chmod u-s,g-s <path>` (or remove its package), or add it to sdw_suid_allowlist with a justification.

controls.title: root is the only UID 0 account
controls.rationale: Any other UID 0 account is an unaccountable, often hidden, root backdoor.
controls.check: /etc/passwd: exactly one account with UID 0, named root.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account

remediation.summary: Delete or renumber the extra UID 0 accounts.
remediation.manual: Investigate first (it may be an intrusion). Then `userdel <name>` or `usermod -u <new_uid> <name>`.

controls.title: No account has an empty password
controls.rationale: An empty password field lets anyone log in as that account locally, and remotely if any service accepts it.
controls.check: /etc/shadow: no account with an empty password field.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure /etc/shadow password fields are not empty

remediation.summary: Lock every account with an empty password (passwd -l).
remediation.risk: The listed accounts can no longer log in until a password is set.

controls.title: All accounts use shadowed passwords
controls.rationale: A hash stored in the world-readable /etc/passwd is exposed to every local user.
controls.check: /etc/passwd: the password field of every account is 'x'.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords

remediation.summary: Move hashes to /etc/shadow with pwconv.

controls.title: No legacy '+' NIS compatibility entries exist
controls.rationale: '+' entries import accounts from NIS, a clear-text directory, and may grant logins with no local record.
controls.check: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group contain no line starting with '+'.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure no legacy "+" entries exist

remediation.summary: Remove the '+' lines.
remediation.manual: Edit the files with vipw / vigr and delete every line starting with '+'.

controls.title: System accounts cannot open a login shell
controls.rationale: Service accounts with a shell can be used interactively if their password or a key leaks.
controls.check: Accounts with UID below UID_MIN (except root, sync, shutdown, halt) have nologin or false as shell.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure system accounts do not have a valid login shell

remediation.summary: Set the shell of those accounts to nologin, except accounts that own a crontab or an authorized_keys file (left for review).
remediation.risk: `su - <account>` no longer opens a shell for those accounts: use `sudo -u <account>` or `runuser`.

controls.title: User and group identifiers are unique
controls.rationale: Shared UIDs/GIDs or duplicate names break accountability and file ownership.
controls.check: /etc/passwd and /etc/group: no duplicate UID, GID, user name or group name.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure no duplicate UIDs exist / Ensure no duplicate GIDs exist / Ensure no duplicate user names exist

remediation.summary: Renumber or remove the duplicates.
remediation.manual: Use usermod -u / groupmod -g, then fix file ownership with find -uid/-gid.

controls.title: Every account's primary group exists
controls.rationale: A dangling GID will be granted to whichever group is created next with that number.
controls.check: Every GID referenced in /etc/passwd exists in /etc/group.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure all groups in /etc/passwd exist in /etc/group

remediation.summary: Create the missing groups or fix the accounts.
remediation.manual: groupadd -g <gid> <name>, or usermod -g <existing_group> <user>.

controls.title: The shadow group has no members
controls.rationale: Members of the shadow group can read every password hash.
controls.check: The shadow group (when present) has no secondary members and is nobody's primary group.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure shadow group is empty

remediation.summary: Remove all members from the shadow group.

controls.title: Home directories are private and correctly owned
controls.rationale: A group- or world-accessible home exposes SSH keys, shell history and credentials; a home owned by someone else lets that person plant files.
controls.check: Each interactive user's home exists, is owned by the user and has mode <= 0750.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure local interactive user home directories are configured

remediation.summary: Remove group-write and all 'other' bits from interactive users' home directories.

controls.title: User dot files cannot be modified by others
controls.rationale: A writable .bashrc or .profile runs attacker code at the victim's next login; .rhosts files grant password-less trust.
controls.check: In each interactive home: no dot file writable by group/other, no .rhosts/.shosts, dot files owned by the user.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure local interactive user dot files access is configured

remediation.summary: Remove group/other write bits from dot files and delete .rhosts/.shosts.

controls.title: Dormant accounts are disabled automatically
controls.rationale: Accounts of people who left are prime targets: nobody notices when they are used.
controls.check: useradd default INACTIVE (/etc/default/useradd) <= sdw_inactive_days_max, and every interactive account with a password, root excepted, has an inactivity limit in /etc/shadow within that bound. Root is exempt: a disabled root account also refuses key logins.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure inactive password lock is configured

remediation.summary: Set the useradd default and the inactivity limit of existing accounts, root excepted; accounts the limit would disable at once are left for review.
remediation.risk: An account whose password expired more than sdw_inactive_days_max days ago is disabled for every login method, keys included.

controls.title: The default umask is restrictive
controls.rationale: With umask 022, every new file (reports, exports, keys) is readable by every user.
controls.check: UMASK in /etc/login.defs and every umask set in /etc/profile, /etc/profile.d/*, /etc/bash.bashrc and /etc/bashrc is sdw_umask or stricter.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure default user umask is configured

remediation.summary: Set UMASK in /etc/login.defs and umask in /etc/profile.d/60-shadow-armor-umask.sh.
remediation.risk: Files users create are no longer readable by other users: shared directories and content deployed by hand may need explicit permissions.

controls.title: Idle interactive shells time out
controls.rationale: An unattended root shell on a console or jump host is a free root session.
controls.check: TMOUT is set to 1..sdw_shell_timeout_max, readonly and exported in a system-wide shell profile.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured

remediation.summary: Write TMOUT to /etc/profile.d/60-shadow-armor-tmout.sh.

actions.content:
# Managed by Shadow-Armor (SA-08.13)
TMOUT={{sdw_shell_timeout_max}}
readonly TMOUT
export TMOUT

remediation.risk: Idle interactive shells close after sdw_shell_timeout_max seconds, root shells and shells inside tmux/screen included.

controls.title: root's primary group is GID 0
controls.rationale: Files created by root must belong to the root group, not to a group that ordinary users may join.
controls.check: The root account's primary GID is 0.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0

remediation.summary: Set root's primary group to 0.

controls.title: Password quality is enforced by PAM
controls.rationale: Settings in pwquality.conf mean nothing unless pam_pwquality (or pam_passwdqc) is in the password stack that passwd uses.
controls.check: Effective PAM password stack (common-password or system-auth, includes expanded) contains pam_pwquality.so, pam_cracklib.so or pam_passwdqc.so.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure pam_pwquality module is enabled

remediation.summary: Install libpam-pwquality (Debian/Ubuntu) or enable pwquality through authselect (RHEL-family).

controls.title: Passwords have a sufficient minimum length
controls.rationale: Length is the single most effective password property against guessing and cracking.
controls.check: Effective minlen (pam_pwquality arguments override pwquality.conf and its drop-ins) >= sdw_password_min_length.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password length is configured

remediation.summary: Set minlen in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/60-shadow-armor.conf.

controls.title: Passwords mix character classes
controls.rationale: Requiring several character classes raises the cost of dictionary attacks against short passwords.
controls.check: Effective minclass (or negative credits) >= sdw_password_min_classes.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password complexity is configured

remediation.summary: Set minclass in the Shadow-Armor pwquality drop-in.

controls.title: Passwords reject repetitions, sequences and dictionary words
controls.rationale: 'aaaaaaaa1', '12345678ab' and dictionary words satisfy length and class rules but fall to the first cracking pass.
controls.check: Effective maxrepeat between 1 and 3, maxsequence between 1 and 3, and dictcheck not disabled.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password same consecutive characters is configured / Ensure password maximum sequential characters is configured / Ensure password dictionary check is enabled

remediation.summary: Set maxrepeat 3, maxsequence 3 and dictcheck 1 in the Shadow-Armor pwquality drop-in.

controls.title: Password quality also applies to root
controls.rationale: Without enforce_for_root, an administrator setting a password for root (or as root for someone else) bypasses the policy.
controls.check: enforce_for_root is set in pwquality.conf, its drop-ins or on the pam_pwquality line.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password quality is enforced for the root user

remediation.summary: Set enforce_for_root in the Shadow-Armor pwquality drop-in.

controls.title: Recent passwords cannot be reused
controls.rationale: Password history stops users from alternating between two known passwords after a forced change.
controls.check: Effective PAM password stack: pam_pwhistory (or pam_unix) with remember >= sdw_password_history.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password history remember is configured

remediation.summary: Enable pam_pwhistory with remember = sdw_password_history (authselect feature on RHEL-family, pam-auth-update profile on Debian/Ubuntu).

controls.title: Passwords are hashed with a strong algorithm
controls.rationale: MD5-crypt and DES-crypt hashes are cracked in minutes on commodity GPUs; yescrypt and SHA-512 crypt are designed to be slow.
controls.check: ENCRYPT_METHOD in /etc/login.defs is YESCRYPT or SHA512, and pam_unix in the effective password stack does not use md5/bigcrypt/blowfish-less legacy options.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure strong password hashing algorithm is configured

remediation.summary: Set ENCRYPT_METHOD to YESCRYPT (Debian/Ubuntu) or SHA512 (RHEL-family) in /etc/login.defs.

controls.title: No stored password uses a weak hash
controls.rationale: Changing the hashing algorithm only affects future passwords: hashes created before still use the old, weak scheme until the password changes.
controls.check: Every password hash in /etc/shadow is yescrypt, SHA-512 crypt, bcrypt or scrypt (MD5-crypt, DES-crypt and SHA-256-crypt fail).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure all current passwords uses the configured hashing algorithm

remediation.summary: Expire the listed passwords so they are re-hashed at next login (chage -d 0).
remediation.risk: The listed users must change their password at next login.

controls.title: Accounts lock after repeated failed logins
controls.rationale: Without lockout, online password guessing is only limited by network speed.
controls.check: Effective PAM auth stack contains pam_faillock (or pam_tally2) with deny between 1 and sdw_lockout_deny_max and unlock_time 0 or >= sdw_lockout_unlock_min (arguments override faillock.conf).

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password failed attempts lockout is configured / Ensure password unlock time is configured

remediation.summary: Enable pam_faillock and set deny/unlock_time in /etc/security/faillock.conf.
remediation.risk: Mistyped passwords lock accounts for the unlock_time; use `faillock --user <name> --reset` to unlock.

controls.title: Passwords expire
controls.rationale: An expiry bound limits how long a leaked password stays useful (PCI requires 90 days when a password is the only factor).
controls.check: PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs <= sdw_password_max_days, and every interactive account with a password, root excepted, has a maximum age within that bound. Root is exempt: an expired root password also blocks key-based root logins until someone types it.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure password expiration is configured

remediation.summary: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS and apply it to existing interactive accounts, root excepted; accounts whose password is already older than the limit are left for review instead of being expired at once.
remediation.risk: Users must change their password before it expires; an expired password blocks key logins too until it is changed.

controls.title: Password changes are rate-limited and announced
controls.rationale: A minimum age stops users from cycling through the history to reuse a password; a warning period avoids surprise lockouts.
controls.check: PASS_MIN_DAYS >= sdw_password_min_days and PASS_WARN_AGE >= sdw_password_warn_days in /etc/login.defs, and existing interactive accounts respect the minimum age.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure minimum password age is configured / Ensure password expiration warning days is configured

remediation.summary: Set PASS_MIN_DAYS and PASS_WARN_AGE and apply them to existing interactive accounts.

controls.title: pam_unix does not accept empty passwords
controls.rationale: The nullok option lets accounts with an empty password authenticate through every PAM-enabled service.
controls.check: No pam_unix.so line in the effective auth/password stacks of common services (login, sshd, su, sudo, passwd) carries nullok.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure pam_unix does not include nullok

remediation.summary: Remove nullok with authselect 'without-nullok' (RHEL-family). On Debian/Ubuntu nullok comes from the package-owned /usr/share/pam-configs/unix profile: remove it there and run pam-auth-update.

controls.title: No security update is pending
controls.rationale: Known, published vulnerabilities with an available fix are the cheapest attack there is.
controls.check: The local package metadata (not refreshed by the audit) lists no pending update from a security source: apt security pockets, dnf/yum updateinfo --security, zypper security patches.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure updates, patches, and additional security software are installed

remediation.summary: Apply pending security updates with the package manager.
remediation.risk: Services restart and a reboot may be needed for kernel and libc updates.

controls.title: Package metadata is fresh
controls.rationale: The security-update check can only see advisories the host has downloaded.
controls.check: The newest repository metadata file (apt lists, dnf/yum repomd.xml) is younger than sdw_metadata_max_age_days.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure package manager repositories are configured

remediation.summary: Refresh the package metadata.

controls.title: Security updates are applied automatically
controls.rationale: Unattended security patching closes the window between disclosure and remediation on hosts nobody patches by hand.
controls.check: Debian/Ubuntu: unattended-upgrades installed and APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists and ::Unattended-Upgrade enabled in the effective apt configuration (`apt-config dump`). RHEL-family: dnf-automatic timer enabled and set to apply updates.

remediation.summary: Install and enable unattended-upgrades (Debian/Ubuntu) or dnf-automatic (RHEL-family) for security updates.

controls.title: Package signatures are verified
controls.rationale: Unsigned or unverified repositories let whoever controls the network path or mirror install code as root.
controls.check: Debian/Ubuntu: no [trusted=yes] source and no AllowUnauthenticated/AllowInsecureRepositories in the effective apt configuration. RHEL-family: gpgcheck=1 in dnf.conf and no repository with gpgcheck=0.

map.cis_benchmark: Ensure GPG keys are configured / Ensure gpgcheck is globally activated

remediation.summary: Re-enable signature checking.
remediation.manual: Debian/Ubuntu: remove [trusted=yes] from sources and APT::Get::AllowUnauthenticated / Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories from /etc/apt/apt.conf.d; import the repository key with signed-by. RHEL-family: set gpgcheck=1 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf and in every /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo, and import the vendor keys.

controls.title: The running kernel is the newest installed
controls.rationale: Installing a kernel update fixes nothing until the host reboots into it: the vulnerable kernel keeps running.
controls.check: Runtime: uname -r. Persistent: newest installed kernel (/boot/vmlinuz-*, rpm install time). A patched-but-not-rebooted host fails with a 'pending' qualifier.

remediation.summary: Reboot into the new kernel.
remediation.manual: Plan a reboot (or use live patching, and waive this control while it covers the pending CVEs).

controls.title: No process still runs replaced libraries
controls.rationale: When a library is patched, processes started before the update keep the old, vulnerable code mapped in memory until restarted.
controls.check: Runtime: /proc/*/maps entries of shared objects marked (deleted).

remediation.summary: Restart the listed services.
remediation.manual: Run `needrestart -r a` (Debian/Ubuntu) or `needs-restarting -s` (RHEL-family) and restart what it lists, or reboot.

controls.title: The operating system release is still supported
controls.rationale: An end-of-life release no longer receives security fixes: every new vulnerability stays open forever.
controls.check: /etc/os-release ID and VERSION_ID compared with the end-of-support table sdw_eol (standard support; waive with justification when covered by paid extended support).

remediation.summary: Upgrade to a supported release.
